history.dynasty: Chola (origin); Western Ganga, Hoysala and Vijayanagara (later contributions); major additions under Hiriya Kempe Gowda II
history.period: Chola period - commonly dated 10th-13th century CE (sources conflict: 9th, 10th-12th, and 12th-13th c. all appear; period CONFLICT - verify)
history.summary: One of Bengaluru's oldest and largest temples, at Halasuru (Ulsoor) beside Ulsoor Lake. It originated in the Chola period (inscriptional and stylistic evidence; the recent discovery of a 1200-year-old kalyani/temple tank during excavations supports deep antiquity) and was greatly expanded in the late Vijayanagara period under Hiriya Kempe Gowda II, when the 48-pillared open mantapa, Nandi shrine, Brahma stambha and the eastern gopuram were added. Legends attribute its consecration to Kempe Gowda (who, while hunting from Yelahanka, dreamed of the deity and built the temple with buried treasure) or to an earlier Yelahanka chief, Jayappa Gowda (1420-1450 CE); another account says the sage Mandavya meditated here (Mandavya Kshetra), and the lingam was once worshipped by sage Markandeya (legends, unverified). The walls carry fine sculptures - Ravana lifting Kailasa, Durga slaying Mahishasura, Girija Kalyana, the Nayanmar saints and the Saptarishis - and the architecture mixes Western Ganga, Chola, Hoysala and Vijayanagara styles. The temple is managed by the Karnataka Muzrai (endowments) department.

name: Sri Someshwara Temple
town_description: Halasuru (older name Ulsoor) is one of Bengaluru's oldest neighbourhoods, just east of the city centre near MG Road and Ulsoor Lake. It was a Tamil-speaking settlement area in the medieval period - a few Mudaliar (Tuluva Vellala) families settled here, leaving Tamil inscriptions in the Someshwara Temple - and today it is a dense central locality served by the Halasuru metro station.
